label: Figure 4.6: PED values for a straight-line demand curve
alt: A straight downward-sloping demand line with points a and b near the top marked PED 4.0 (elastic) and points c and d near the bottom marked PED 0.67 (inelastic).
caption: On the straight-line demand curve P = 25 − Q/10, moving from a (50, $20) to b (70, $18) gives a 40% rise in quantity for a 10% fall in price, so PED = 4.0 (elastic). Moving from c (150, $10) to d (170, $8) gives a 13.3% rise in quantity for a 20% fall in price, so PED = 0.67 (inelastic). Elasticity falls as we move down the same straight line.
